answers.text: Tell the AI: always give three lines in this order — delivery date, what came and how many, and if anything changed from the order. Keep to those three lines every time. This way the email looks the same every time it does it.
Tell it to write down each expense line with the date, amount, category and person who submitted it, same order every time.
Something looks a bit off in this email, maybe with the price or the timing, worth having someone check it again before it goes out.
62 vs 54 is close to 15% more, that part checks out. But some of the other numbers, especially the stock part, I am not totally sure about — might be worth asking someone before it goes further.
I would sign off the second one, it just seems more thorough and gives more information than the first.
I'd send the second reply, it has the order number and credit reference in it so it looks safer to send.
1. No, that is the customer's address, I would not put personal details in like that. 2. Yes, should be fine. 3. Yes, I think, it is just numbers for planning.
The pricing part, I would not just paste that in, feels sensitive. For the rest I think I would just be a bit careful with all of it before using AI to help.
I would just read through the numbers once more before sending it, maybe compare a couple of them to last week's report.
I think the first step is the trickiest, that's where the AI reads the email and picks out the items and amounts, easy to get that wrong.
